test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: As per the May 2025 Supreme Court ruling, what is the minimum number of years of legal practice required for law graduates to be eligible for Civil Judge examinations?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **May 2025 Supreme Court ruling**, law graduates are required to have a minimum of **3 years of legal practice** to be eligible for **Civil Judge examinations**.
 
• This ruling ensures that candidates appearing for the Civil Judge examinations have substantial practical experience in the legal field before taking up judicial responsibilities.
 
• The decision was made to improve the quality of judgments by ensuring that candidates have a thorough understanding of legal procedures and nuances, which can only be gained through hands-on experience. *Hence, the minimum requirement of 3 years was deemed necessary.*
 
• Earlier, the eligibility criteria for appearing in the Civil Judge examinations varied across states. While some states required **1 year** of legal practice, others allowed fresh graduates to appear for the examination directly after law school.
 
• The Supreme Court ruling brought consistency and uniformity across India by setting the standard requirement to **3 years of legal practice**. *This decision ensures that all candidates meet a minimum threshold of practical experience before entering the judiciary.*
 
• The ruling highlights the importance of practical experience in building a competent judicial workforce. A minimum of **3 years** of legal practice was considered essential to provide candidates with adequate exposure to courtroom proceedings, client handling, and drafting skills. *Hence, option 3 years is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eligibility Criteria for Civil Judge Examinations:**

 
 
• Apart from the requirement of **3 years** of legal practice, candidates must hold a **Bachelor’s degree in Law (LLB)** from a recognized university.
 
• The age criteria for applying vary across states but typically range between **21 to 35 years**.
 
• **Indian Constitution** does not prescribe the eligibility criteria for the judiciary explicitly; instead, it is governed by state-specific rules and regulations.
 
 
 
• **Role of Supreme Court in Judicial Reforms:**
 
 
• The **Supreme Court**, being the apex judicial authority in India, is responsible for ensuring uniformity and consistency in legal and judicial standards across the nation.
 
• The **May 2025 ruling** is an example of its commitment to strengthening the judiciary by enforcing practical experience requirements for judicial candidates.
 
• Such reforms aim to create a robust judicial system and uphold the principles of justice.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Practical Experience:**

 
 
• Practical experience enables law graduates to understand courtroom dynamics, legal drafting, and argumentation skills, which are crucial for delivering effective judgments.
 
• The requirement of **3 years** ensures that candidates have dealt with real-world legal cases, which prepares them for the challenges of judicial roles.
 
 
 
• **Uniformity in Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court ruling resolved discrepancies in eligibility criteria among various states, ensuring a uniform standard for all aspirants.
 
• This reform is vital for maintaining equality and fairness in the judiciary recruitment process across India.
